scenario_text: Arterial carbon dioxide and oxygen tensions are independently clamped while steady minute ventilation is measured in a resting subject. The target is the integrated ventilatory output of central and peripheral chemoreceptor drive under fixed metabolic demand. Ventilation rises with carbon dioxide and is amplified when oxygen tension becomes low, but respiratory motor output has a finite physiological ceiling. Acid-base adaptation and temporal response delays are excluded from the baseline experiment.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent adds a CO2 term with one fixed gain to a hypoxic sigmoid term before motor saturation, so at any fixed P_O2 the pre-saturation CO2 sensitivity is proportional to a single constant G_CO2 and does not depend on hypoxic drive.
response_change.child_relation: Make effective CO2 chemosensitivity increase with hypoxic receptor activation, so the slope of ventilation versus P_CO2 becomes steeper when P_O2 is low even before the common motor-output saturation acts.
response_change.observable_effect: Across CO2 clamps spanning the sampled range, the rise of V_E with P_CO2 is modest in normoxia but distinctly steeper in hypoxia; the parent cannot create this O2-dependent CO2 slope change with one shared parameter set because P_O2 only adds an offset before saturation.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when measurements include both relatively normoxic and clearly hypoxic P_O2 values, with P_CO2 varied away from zero so that changes in CO2 slope can be estimated before V_E is pinned near V_E_max; strongest for low P_O2 where H_O2 is appreciable and moderate total drive where saturation is incomplete.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, low-P_O2 subsets already show amplified CO2 responsiveness relative to high-P_O2 subsets; in holdout, extending to more severe hypoxia strengthens the same monotone amplification rather than introducing a new regime.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the hypoxia-dependent modulation strength tends to zero, so CO2 gain becomes effectively constant again.
plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes central CO2 chemosensitivity has a single fixed gain independent of oxygenation, omitting the established multiplicative potentiation of ventilatory CO2 responsiveness during hypoxia.
plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that CO2 and hypoxic chemoreceptor drives combine only additively before motor saturation with a P_O2-independent CO2 gain.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Peripheral hypoxic activation augments the effective responsiveness of the ventilatory controller to arterial CO2, producing hypercapnic-hypoxic synergy in steady ventilation.
plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: at fixed P_O2, V_E increases monotonically with P_CO2, but the local pre-saturation CO2 drive uses one constant gain G_CO2; changing P_O2 mainly shifts total drive upward through the additive hypoxia term and then may compress responses only via the final common saturation. Child change: low P_O2 increases the CO2-response slope itself through a monotone interaction between the hypoxic activation fraction and the CO2 term. Distinguishing condition: vary P_CO2 across several clamp levels while holding P_O2 first in a normoxic range and then in a hypoxic range; compare the V_E-versus-P_CO2 slope at matched unsaturated ventilation levels. Under admissible conditions with appreciable but not maximal hypoxic activation and without complete motor saturation, the child predicts steeper hypercapnic sensitivity in hypoxia, whereas the parent with a single shared parameter set cannot independently alter CO2 slope by P_O2 except indirectly through ceiling compression, which tends to reduce apparent slope near saturation rather than selectively amplify it at low P_O2. This is a changed target mapping from supplied inputs P_CO2 and P_O2 to V_E, not merely an auxiliary reformulation. Limitation: if all observations lie very near V_E_max or all P_O2 values remain well above the hypoxic transition, the interaction would be weakly identifiable.

evolution_contracts.observable_signature: At fixed moderate P_CO2 variation and incomplete saturation, V_E-versus-P_CO2 curves fan out by oxygenation: normoxic curves have lower slope, while hypoxic curves are steeper even at matched submaximal drive. evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all parent parameters cannot reproduce this across both normoxic and hypoxic conditions with one shared parameter set because in the parent the derivative of the unsaturated drive with respect to P_CO2 is always G_CO2/P_CO2_ref, independent of P_O2. response_change.parent_relation: The hypoxic contribution and hypoxic potentiation of CO2 sensitivity share one fixed oxygen half-activation P_O2_half, so changing P_CO2 only rescales drive amplitude without shifting the apparent oxygen threshold of the ventilatory rise.
response_change.child_relation: Allow the oxygen half-activation governing peripheral chemoreflex recruitment to depend on P_CO2, so hypercapnia shifts the oxygen-response curve left or right and changes where hypoxic amplification becomes prominent, not just how large it becomes.
response_change.observable_effect: When comparing V_E versus P_O2 curves at low versus high fixed P_CO2, the child can show a CO2-dependent displacement of the hypoxic knee in addition to gain change; the parent can only change slope/amplitude around one common oxygen threshold.
